commentary_title: Aframax market softens amid lower congestion and weak tonne-miles
commentary_summary: Aframax utilisation eased to 89.9% during Week 39, down 1 percentage point MoM and YoY, while the tonne-mile index remained weak at 90.7, down 12.1% YoY. Lower tonne-mile demand continues to weigh on market, although utilisation remains close to the key 90% level, suggesting fleet employment is still relatively healthy. | East of Suez remained the stronger market, with the share of laden vessels rising by 3.6 percentage points MoM, reflecting steady cargo activity. However, declining anchored capacity and higher ballast speeds suggest vessel availability is improving as fleet repositioning outpaces demand growth, reducing market tightness across key loading regions. | Congestion continued to ease across major trading regions, supporting faster vessel turnaround and higher fleet productivity. Lower anchorage levels, particularly in Asian discharge areas, combined with elevated sailing speeds despite higher bunker prices, effectively increased available tonnage and limited support for spot freight rates.
